newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria adopts austerity draft budget for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Algeria adopts austerity draft budget for 1997.

text.p: The Algerian government on Wednesday adopted a draft budget for 1997 which perseveres with austerity policies aimed at taming inflation, Algerian state-run radio said.
"Austerity measures carried out in line with readjusting the budget in 1996 will be maintained in 1997," said the radio, quoting a cabinet statement.
The radio gave no figures for expected expenditure and revenue for 1997 but said the budget would focus on investment in economic sectors like housing, agriculture and energy.

"The internal debt will be settled by the state budget resources for the first time, reflecting the significance of the state efforts aimed to generate public savings in the framework of rigour and discipline," the radio said.
"Investment in equipment will increase by 10 percent in the 1997 budget," it added.
The government-appointed Transitional National Council, a quasi-parliament, will vote on the budget when it resumes its 100-day session on Saturday.
The radio said the government also will reconfigure the tax system in the draft budget.
The government had forecasted a budget for 1996, with a total expenditure of 848.6 billion dinars ($15.7 billion) and revenue totalling 749.2 billion ($13.8 billion).
Algeria is grappling with civil strife in which an estimated 50,000 people have been killed since early 1992.
